To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The tumor stroma is a dynamic structure that is generated by a complex interplay between malignant cells, the host immune response, and the tumor microenvironment.
(1) The tumor microenvironment is a key factor in cancer progression, and (2) the tumor microenvironment can be manipulated for the benefit of the patient.

(1) the tumor microenvironment (TME) is composed of a variety of cell types, including cancer cells and non-cancerous cells, such as immune cells, stromal cells, and endothelial cells, and extracellular matrix components; (2) the TME is a dynamic environment that is constantly changing in response to the tumor and the surrounding environment, and (3) the TME plays a crucial role in tumor progression, metastasis, and treatment response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the extracellular matrix (ECM) and its associated proteins, the proteoglycans and the glycosaminoglycans in the regulation of cell growth and differentiation.
the molecular mechanisms of wound healing and tumor growth, and how to apply this knowledge to improve the treatment of chronic wounds and to prevent tumor growth
the molecular mechanisms that regulate tumor cell invasion, metastasis, and angiogenesis

tumor cells are the result of a series of genetic mutations that cause the cell to grow out of control.
the wound healing process is a very complex process that requires a lot of time and effort to heal.
the similarities between the tumor stroma and wound healing are not sufficient to explain the process of cancer metastasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the stromal cells in a tumour can be reprogrammed to a state that promotes tumour growth and metastasis.
tumor growth and metastasis are not only dependent on cancer cell proliferation and survival but are also dependent on the tumor microenvironment.
the wound healing model is not a good model for the tumor stroma and that the tumor stroma is a better model for wound healing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the wound healing response can be a double-edged sword in the tumor microenvironment, and that the tumor microenvironment can also influence the wound healing response.
